messages:
incident-bot: P99 latency spike detected on /v1/chat/completions in us-west-2. 5min p99 = 1.8s, baseline p99 = 320ms. alert: LR-CHAT-P99-ROUTE

sam: paging rota — I'm on it. Paging @anya (platform oncall) and @tj (runtime).

anya: oncall here. seen the alert. pulling recent traces and partial QPS.

tj: I'll check model routing and pool saturation. any customer-facing errors?

sam: not many 500s, but slow tails. user-facing increases in latency for a small subset of routes (conversation-heavy). traces show long KV cache misses for longer contexts.

paul: can we temporarily route to the lower-latency model variant for the heavy conversation route? e.g., fallback to gpt-like-compat-v1-lite

kevin: we can, but that has slightly different tokenization. risk: slight drift in outputs. mitigation: short canary (5m) + automated rollback.

maria: ops-bot started a spike dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/1722001234 - looks like a per-model hot spot on model-id: rw-chat-8k-qa.

tj: running command to scale dedicated pool for rw-chat-8k-qa:
```
redwoodctl pool scale --pool rw-chat-8k-qa --replicas 4
```

sam: doing the route override for the next 10m to shift 40% of traffic to rw-chat-8k-compat. doing canary with header flag.

anya: note: suppressing LR-CHAT-P99-ROUTE for 15m to avoid noisy pages while mitigation in flight. created temp suppress in alerting UI. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Suppression created by anya for LR-CHAT-P99-ROUTE until +900s

kevin: pool scaled, canary in place. can we watch p95/p99 on the per-route dashboard?

maria: updated dashboard with synthetic for the route and per-model p95/p99. initial numbers after shift: p95=220ms, p99=360ms (improved).

sam: good. next steps: post-incident followup to reduce noisy alerts and move to per-model thresholds. who owns that?

paul: I can drive the alert tuning doc. propose: move LR-CHAT-P99-ROUTE to per-route-per-model policy with adaptive thresholds based on recent baseline (30d rolling) + a static floor. idea: p95 threshold = baseline_p95 * 1.6, p99 threshold = baseline_p99 * 2.0, min floors: p95=150ms, p99=300ms.

tj: also recommend splitting multi-tenant routes: conversation-heavy routes get stricter p95 but looser p99 tolerances because of long contexts; embed-only routes keep tight p99.

anya: action items:
- paul: write RFC for per-route-per-model alerting + runbook (deadlines: propose by EOD tomorrow)
- kevin: add per-model series to Grafana + alert templates (ETA 2d)
- tj: investigate KV cache misses and propose runtime fix (ETA 3d)
- sam: update oncall playbook with temporary suppression steps + paging thresholds (ETA EOD today)

kevin: quick sketch of the new alert rule (we'll formalize in terraform):
```
alert: CHAT_ROUTE_P99_PER_MODEL
expr: max_over_time(route_model_latency_p99[5m]) > (baseline_p99 * 2.0) and baseline_p99 > 0
for: 5m
labels: {severity: "page", owner: "platform"}
annotations: {runbook: "https://wiki.redwood/alerts/chat-p99"}
```

maria: note for postmortem: surface customer impact: we saw 24 distinct API keys with >250ms increase in median latency, two customers reported degraded app UX, no SLA breaches.

anya: can we add a short automated customer-impact query to the incident runbook to check top affected API keys and flag sales/CS?

sam: yes — add a `top_api_key_latency` step that runs a quick aggregation and posts results to incident channel + pings CS. I added a template in the runbook.

ops-bot: Runbook step executed: top_api_key_latency -> keys: key_abc, key_def, key_xyz; top_api_key = key_abc (p99 increase 980ms)

paul: I'll include that automated check in the RFC. Also propose an alert damping period: new alerts that trip within 10m of a suppression won't page unless they exceed 2x threshold. reduces churn during mitigations.

tj: agree. small procedural note: ensure we don't suppress for long-running degradations; suppression must be tied to an incident id and expire automatically.

sam: thanks all. lifting suppression in 10m unless we see a regression. I'll open the RFC and link to this thread.

maria: postmortem link (placeholder): https://wiki.redwood/incidents/1722001234-latency-tail - feel free to add logs and dashboards. :spiral_notepad:

kevin: after-action note: consider per-model quantization profiles — some models have disproportionate CPU usage causing tail latency. add to Optimize backlog.

anya: closing loop: suppression removed at +900s. final metrics after mitigation (30m window): route p95=200ms (baseline 170ms), p99=340ms (baseline 320ms). incident resolved, will continue follow-ups in RFC. :tada:
